{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=methods+for+ensuring+full-chain+traceability+and+accountability+in+autonomous+scientific+discovery+loops&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1038/s41598-026-63360-y\", \"title\": [\"Ensuring food supply chain transparency through blockchain-driven traceability\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n                  <jats:p>\\n                    Food supply chains face increasing challenges related to transparency, traceability, and data integrity. This study proposes a blockchain-based traceability framework integrating the\\n                    <jats:italic>InterPlanetary File System (IPFS)</jats:italic>\\n                    , Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, and a hybrid GM-PBFT consensus mechanism to ensure secure and efficient data sharing across stakeholders. The proposed system combines on-chain and off-chain storage to reduce blockchain overhead while preserving data immutability. A MobileNetV1-based model is incorporated for product quality assessment. Experimental evaluation using Hyperledger Fabric and Ethereum test networks demonstrates improved performance, achieving 99.3% traceability accuracy, 37% faster recall response, and reduced data tampering risk. The results confirm that the proposed approach enhances transparency, scalability, and trust in agri-food supply chains. The proposed system utilizes a hybrid blockchain architecture, combining\\n                    <jats:italic>Hyperledger Fabric (permissioned blockchain)</jats:italic>\\n                    for secure enterprise-level transactions and\\n                    <jats:italic>Ethereum Layer-2 network</jats:italic>\\n                    for scalability and smart contract execution.\\n                  </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-63360-y\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 7]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7546940\", \"title\": [\"Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Scientific Discovery: Autonomous Research, Human Oversight, Accountability, and the Transformation of Knowledge Creation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Agentic artificial intelligence is extending research automation from individual predictions and laboratory operations to sequences of scientific decisions. This structured critical narrative review examines which activities have been delegated, how resulting claims are validated, and what arrangements can preserve human oversight and accountability. A purposive, nonexhaustive search of scholarly and official sources was updated through 30 September 2026. The analysis compares robotic experimentation, tool-using language agents, automated computational research, and systems for generating and refining hypotheses. Demonstrations establish useful capacities within specified environments, but neither workflow completion nor automated assessment establishes general scientific competence. The review distinguishes operational autonomy, evidential justification, and institutional authority, showing why these dimensions must be evaluated separately. It argues for intervention at consequential decision boundaries, independent checks matched to the type of claim, and records linking evidence, tool actions, permissions, and human responsibility. The supplied healthcare explainability paper informs the discussion of calibrated reliance, with its application to scientific agents treated as an analytical extension. Knowledge creation is examined as an institutional process involving validation, criticism, attribution, and reuse, rather than merely the production of candidate findings. The contribution is an integrative comparison and research agenda, not a validated new framework or an empirical estimate of field-wide performance. Generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, substantially assisted literature organization, synthesis, drafting, and preparation of tables and figures; the author must independently review and approve the sources, arguments, and manuscript before submission.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7546940\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.55041/ijsrem46173\", \"title\": [\"A Study on Traceability and Accountability in Supply Chain Transparency Using Blockchain Technology\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>ABSTRACT\\nThis article explores the critical importance of traceability and accountability within modern supply chains, and how blockchain technology provides innovative solutions to enhance transparency and trust. Drawing upon literature, case studies, and emerging practices, the study identifies the transformative potential of distributed ledger technology (DLT) in tackling issues such as product authenticity, fraud, and ethical sourcing.
